title: India Smartphone Shipments Fall 20% to Decade Low in Q3
excerpt: Counterpoint Research says record-high memory prices pushed up device costs, sub-Rs 20,000 shipments fell 47%, and Samsung reclaimed the top spot with a 17% share.
body:
• India's smartphone shipments fell 20% year on year in Q3 2026 to their lowest level in a decade, according to Counterpoint Research.
  • Shipments below Rs 20,000 fell 47% as record-high memory prices pushed models into higher price bands and buyers deferred upgrades.
  • Samsung reclaimed the top spot after nine quarters with a 17% share and was the only top-five brand to grow year on year; vivo was second on 16%.
  • Counterpoint expects India's market to shrink about 13% in 2026, with another round of price hikes likely after the festive season sale.

India's smartphone shipments fell 20% year on year in the July-September quarter to their lowest level in a decade, according to Counterpoint Research's Monthly India Smartphone Tracker. Record-high memory prices drove up device costs, demand stayed soft, and manufacturers held back channel inventory even ahead of the festive season.

The damage was concentrated at the affordable end. Shipments priced below Rs 20,000 declined 47% in Q3 2026, nearly halving, as rising model prices pushed devices into higher price bands, Counterpoint said.

"Q3 marked a realignment for India's smartphone market, as a memory-led cost squeeze compounded softer consumer demand."

— Shubham Singh, Research Analyst, Counterpoint Research

Why the mass market stalled

Research analyst Shubham Singh said rising component costs put pressure on affordability and weakened the traditional mass-market volume engine, particularly below Rs 15,000. Consumers became more selective, extended replacement cycles and deferred upgrades. Manufacturers, in turn, prioritised margin protection, portfolio rationalisation and leaner channel inventory over aggressive volume expansion ahead of Diwali.

The adjustment is already visible in product line-ups. Counterpoint said brands are introducing more 4G and lower-specification models and trading down specifications in some segments to hold price points. For buyers, that means the same budget may buy less memory or a weaker specification than a year earlier, even when the headline price looks unchanged.

Brand standings

Samsung reclaimed the top spot after nine quarters with a 17% share. Counterpoint credited the Galaxy A series, a balanced online and offline strategy, relatively measured price hikes and proactive management of memory costs. Its eighth-generation foldables, using a passport-style form factor for the first time, also gained traction. Samsung was the only player among the top five to register year-on-year growth.

vivo, excluding iQOO, was second with 16%, with the Y series driving volume while the T series stayed under pressure. OPPO held third with 12%, driven by triple-digit growth above Rs 20,000. Xiaomi, including POCO, was also on 12% and was the top brand in the Rs 10,001-Rs 20,000 band. Apple saw a strong start for the iPhone 18 Pro series, with initial sales nearly 20% higher year on year than the iPhone 17 Pro series.

Smaller brands moved faster from a low base. Ai+ Smartphone was the fastest-growing brand, up 306% year on year. Indian brands' combined share rose from 2% in Q3 2025 to 7% in Q3 2026, Transsion's itel grew 88% on its 4G portfolio below Rs 15,000, and Google grew more than 50%. MediaTek remained the leading chipset supplier with a 45% share.

The numbers in one place

The quarter amounts to a price shock, not a collapse in interest in smartphones. Volumes fell because the entry point moved. A segment that supplied the market's volume — phones below Rs 20,000, and especially below Rs 15,000 — shrank by almost half in a single year, while premium and upper-mid demand held up better and brands such as OPPO grew above Rs 20,000.

Outlook

"We expect India's smartphone market to shrink by around 13% in 2026, with continued pricing pressure weighing on affordability and replacement demand."

— Tarun Pathak, Research Director, Counterpoint Research

Research director Tarun Pathak said the post-festive seasonal slowdown will add pressure, and elevated component costs are likely to drive another round of price hikes after the festive season sale. Counterpoint expects the market to remain on a challenging footing entering 2027, with growth shifting toward premium and upper-mid segments.

With upfront prices rising, no-cost EMIs, exchange offers and retailer-led promotions will become more important in converting buyers who still need to upgrade. For manufacturers, the strategic question is whether to protect margins with higher prices and leaner inventory, or defend share in a mass market whose economics memory prices have abruptly changed.
